full_judgment:
Mohammad Fazlul Karim J:- The defendant is the appellant in this appeal where in the leave was granted to consider the submissions of the learned Counsel for the appellant that the defendant appellant having already paid the admitted principal decreetal amount of TK. 2,24,72,280/- to the plaintiff but by the decree the appellant has been illegally saddled with an interstate the rate of 18% without any basis or supporting materials and the date from which the interest would accrue. The learned Counsel further contends that the order of maintaining interest @ 18% on account of two final bills for a sum of TK. 2,24,72,280/- and for direction to pay the entire decreetal amount of TK. 5,35,24,852/- within three months from the date of judgment and decree with 18% interest till realization is arbitrary, whimsical, collusive and exorbitant which cannot be sustained. 

 4. After examination of both oral and documentary evidence the trial Court decreed the suit directing that the plaintiff' is entitled to an amount of TK. 6,35,24,852/ with interest @ 18% till realization. 

 5. The defendant then moved the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 159 of 1998 and a Division Bench by judgment dated 31.1.2000 allowed the appeal in part setting aside the decree for Tk. 1,00,00,000/- awarded as compensation but the judgment and decree of the trial Court relating to TK. 2,24,72,280/-and interest of TK. 3,10,52,572/ totaling TK. 5,35,24,852/- was affirmed. 

 6. The suit was decreed by the trial Court for an amount of TK. 6,35,24,852/- with interest @ 18% till realization but on appeal an amount of TK. 1,00,00,000/ awarded as compensation was set aside maintaining the decree for principal amount of TK. 2,24,72,280/. and interest of TK. 3,10,52,572/- totaling TK. 5,35,24,852/- as affirmed to be paid within three months from date with interest 55 18% till realization thereof. 

 7. The appellant has taken exception to the awarding of the interest at the rate of 18% till realization. Section 34 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides that payment of interest is discretionary but should not be refused in the absence of proper reason and in exercising discretion it must be reasonable. The rate of interest should also be equitable in the facts and circumstances of the case. The exercise of discretion depends on many facts including the fact that the amount decreed was in respect of a liability arising out of a commercial transaction. 

 9. The respondents has referred to two bank documents supported by oral evidence to show that the plaintiff respondent has utilized the amount in the contract work taking loan from a Bank @ 18% and has been incurring interest in the said loan amount @ 18% until realization in Title Suit No. 255 of 1997 filed against the respondent which has been decreed with interest @ 18% . But in the instant case the Court has allowed simple interest to be paid by the appellant at the rate of 18% till realization. Since the respondents are also obliged to pay the loan taken from the Bank for utilizing the amount in the contract work at the rate of 18% compound interest, ends of justice would be best served if the appellant is directed to pay interest at the rate of 18% in respect of the deereetal amount till realization. The High Court Division also found that the interest calculated and awarded by the trial Court is maintainable and there is no evidence to show that awarding or calculating of such interest is against any agreement or against any interest on record.
